title: Problem Solving & Coding Patterns in Go
intro: Problem-solving and coding patterns in Go cover the programs every Go fresher is asked to write in a 30-minute screening. This module covers seven canonical problems written idiomatically in Go: FizzBuzz (the baseline — if it takes more than 3 minutes something is wrong, but showing clean switch and string conversion matters), Fibonacci (iterative with a simple loop vs recursive — and why iterative is preferred in Go for stack-depth reasons), palindrome check (rune-safe using a slice of runes, not indexing bytes), anagram check (using a frequency map with make(map[rune]int)), two-sum (the hash map approach, O(n) time — the Go map literal and the ok pattern for existence check), reverse a string rune-safely (range + append to a rune slice + string()), and word count (strings.Fields + a map, the range-over-string gotcha). Every solution is complete, compiles, and is written the way a Go developer writes it — not Java or Python style with Go syntax bolted on. The meta-lesson: interviewers watch how you use the language, not just whether you get the right answer.
